chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Yazeed al-Nakha'i, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I saw a man in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the lesbian with the lesbian?' He said to him, 'I will not inform you until you swear that you will inform the women with what I inform you with.' He said, so he swore an oath for him. He said, then he said: 'They are both in the Fire, and upon them are seventy garments of Fire. Above those garments is a dry, thick skin of Fire. Upon them are two belts of Fire and two crowns of Fire above those garments, and two shoes of Fire, and they are both in the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on female homosexuality in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the severe eschatological punishment for female homosexuality (al-lawati), emphasizing its gravity through vivid imagery of layered fire garments. The requirement of an oath from the companion Bashir al-Nabbal to ensure the message was conveyed to women highlights the practical transmission of this specific legal ruling within early Shia scholarly circles. This narration serves as a key textual evidence for the distinct penal status of this act in Shia fiqh, distinguishing it through the specificity of its described torments.
